title: Why 'Healthy' Food Labels Don't Tell the Whole Story
paragraphs: These claims look great when we see them on the labels of food or drinks we hope to buy. But do they mean these products are actually healthier?
Well, probably. But not always. And maybe not as much as we'd like.

Researchers at Cornell University and the University of Kentucky looked at almost 150,000 food products in the US. They found that foods that make health claims on their packaging are generally healthier than those that don't make such claims — but not always.
The study looked at food products that were launched in the US between January 2015 and December 2024.

The foods and drinks were judged using a scoring system developed in the UK called the "Nutrient Profiling Model." This scoring system gives positive points for things like sugar, salt and saturated fat, and negative points for things like fiber and protein, with a higher score being worse for health.
Under this system, foods with a score of four or higher are considered "less healthy," as are drinks with a score of one or more.

When the researchers applied this system to US food and drinks, they found that two-thirds of products launched from 2015 to 2024 would be considered "less healthy" — even though half had health claims on their packaging.
The researchers also found that reducing one unhealthy ingredient sometimes just meant adding more of a different one.

And while foods with health labels were generally healthier than those without, drinks were less consistent. In particular, drink labels like "reduced sodium" and "low in saturated fat" sometimes meant these drinks had more sugar to compensate for the ingredients that had been removed.
The researchers were also concerned that labels like "organic" and "all natural" may sound healthy, but don't actually say anything about a product's sugar, salt or fat content.
The researchers said their results show that shoppers should look at more than just the health claims on the front of packaging, and should read the full nutrition information on the back too.
